transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess the main reason is I’m just… exhausted all the time. Not just tired like I stayed up too late, but worn out in this heavy, whole-body way. I can sleep a full night and still wake up feeling like my body is made of sandbags, like everything takes so much effort before the day has even started.

It’s gotten to where getting through work feels like I’m dragging myself from one thing to the next, and I work in marketing research, so I need to think clearly and stay focused, and even that feels like climbing a hill some days. And then when I get home, something small like folding laundry or putting things away can feel completely overwhelming, like it takes everything I have. I just don’t feel like myself, and I’m tired of feeling this drained all the time.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yeah… I have. Most days, honestly. It’s not always like I’m crying or anything dramatic like that, but I wake up and there’s this heavy, flat feeling in my chest before I’ve even really started the day. Like I’ll sit at the kitchen table with my coffee, just staring out at the yard, and everything feels kind of colorless.

And I get this thought—not exactly in words every time, but it’s there—that there isn’t some better version of my life waiting up ahead. Like I can’t picture a future where I feel lighter or excited about things. It just feels like more of the same, and that scares me, because I don’t think I used to feel that way so much.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I have, pretty noticeably. I used to be pretty good about making time for things that felt like mine, you know? Like hiking on weekends, or going to yoga, or working in my garden after work when the weather was decent. And I used to really like taking photos of birds—nothing professional, just with my camera, walking around and trying to catch them in the yard or on trails.

But lately it’s like… even thinking about doing those things feels like too much effort. I’ll tell myself I should go for a hike because I know I used to enjoy it, and then I’ll end up canceling or just not going. My yoga mat is just sitting there. The garden is kind of neglected, which makes me feel bad, because that used to calm me down. And my camera has been sitting in the closet for I don’t even know how long. I look at it and think, “I should take it out,” but then it just feels pointless somehow, like it wouldn’t be worth the energy.

It’s not that I suddenly hate those things. It’s more like they don’t pull me toward them anymore. They feel far away, like things a different version of me used to care about.
Have you been having thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of wanting to die?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to say it too strongly, because that makes it feel more real, but… yes, I’ve had thoughts like that.

It’s usually late at night, when everything is quiet and my husband is asleep, and I’m just lying there staring at the ceiling. My mind starts going to this really dark place where I think maybe he’d be better off without me. Like I’m just this weight in the house, or I’m making everything harder by being the way I am right now.

I haven’t made a plan or anything like that. I need to say that clearly. It’s not like I’ve sat down and figured something out. But the thought keeps coming back, and that’s what scares me. It’s not just a passing thing that happened once. It feels like it’s been showing up enough that I don’t feel like I can just brush it off anymore.
Before this current stretch, have you ever had another period in your life when you felt depressed like this for a couple of weeks or longer?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean… I’ve had times where I was sad or worn down, like anyone, I guess, but I don’t know if I’d call it the same as this, or if it lasted a full couple of weeks in that way.

I’m trying to think back and it all gets a little blurry, honestly. There were stretches where I felt low or kind of shut down, but I don’t know if I was actually depressed like this or if I was just stressed and tired. I don’t want to say yes and make it sound more definite than it is. This current stretch feels more noticeable to me, more… like it’s settled in.
After physical or mental activity, do you tend to feel markedly worse afterward?

Yes… I think so. Or, maybe it’s not always like a dramatic crash after one specific thing, but activity definitely seems to wipe me out in a way that doesn’t feel normal for me.

Honestly, feeling worn out all the time is a big part of why I came in. Even if I’ve been in bed for a full night, I’ll get up and it’s like my body is made of sandbags. Like everything is heavy before the day has even started. And then if I do anything that takes effort—work especially, trying to focus through the day, answering emails, analyzing reports, sitting in meetings—it just drains me completely. By the time I’m done, I don’t feel like I’ve just worked a normal day. I feel like I’ve been wrung out.

Even things at home, like folding laundry or putting dishes away, can feel like this huge production. I’ll start something small and then have to sit down, not because it’s physically hard in the usual sense, but because it feels like I just don’t have anything in the tank. It’s embarrassing to say, because these are basic things, but getting through them takes everything I have lately.
When you wake up in the morning, do you usually feel refreshed?

No, not really. I mean, I can be in bed for what should be a full night, and when I wake up it doesn’t feel like I’ve rested. It’s more like I’m just… coming back online already exhausted.

My body feels so heavy in the morning, like I’m made of sandbags or something. I’ll lie there thinking about getting up, and even that feels like it takes effort. And then once I do get moving, it’s not like I shake it off after coffee or a shower. It kind of follows me through the day.

That’s honestly a big reason I came in. I feel worn out all the time. Getting through work takes everything out of me, and then even simple things at home, like folding laundry, feel like this huge task. So no, I wouldn’t say I wake up refreshed. I wake up feeling like I’m already behind on energy before I’ve even started.
Have you been unusually sensitive to cold lately?

I don’t think so. I mean, I haven’t really noticed anything unusual like that.

I do get cold sometimes, but I think it’s more normal stuff, like if the office air conditioning is too high or I’m sitting still for a while. I haven’t had a moment where I thought, “Wow, why am I freezing when everyone else is fine?” At least not that I can clearly remember.

So… no, I wouldn’t say I’ve been unusually sensitive to cold lately.
Have you been worrying a lot more than usual about different parts of your life?

I’m not sure I’d put it as “worrying a lot more,” exactly. I mean, I do think about things—work, money, whether I’m keeping up with everything, that kind of normal life stuff—but I don’t know that it feels like this big separate thing where I’m constantly worrying across every part of my life.

It’s more like… I notice when I’m already worn down, my thoughts can get more repetitive, like I’ll go over what I still need to do or whether I’m falling behind. But I’m not sure if that’s worry in the way you mean, or just me trying to keep track of everything and feeling like I don’t have enough bandwidth.

So I guess my answer is: maybe a little at times, but I haven’t really noticed a major increase in worrying about lots of different areas.
How long have you been feeling this depressed and drained most days?

I’d say it’s been about two months now, most days. It didn’t feel like it started all at once, like one morning I woke up and everything was different, but looking back, that’s about when this depressed, slowed-down, drained feeling really became the usual.

At first I think I kept telling myself it was just a rough week, or that I was tired from work, or maybe I just needed a weekend to catch up. But then the weekends didn’t really reset anything, and the next week would start and I’d still feel the same. So… yeah, about the past two months is probably the clearest answer. Most days during that time I’ve felt low and just kind of exhausted in a way that feels hard to push through.
After even mild physical or mental activity, do you often have a delayed crash where your exhaustion gets clearly worse and lasts into the next day or longer?

I don’t think I’ve noticed that pattern, no. I definitely get tired after doing things, especially if I’ve already been feeling drained that day, but I’m not sure I’d call it a delayed crash.

Like, if I have a busy workday or I have to concentrate for a long stretch, I might feel more worn out afterward, but it seems more immediate or just part of the same general exhaustion. I can’t really point to a clear thing where I do something mild—like a short errand or a bit of mental effort—and then the next day I’m dramatically worse because of that specific activity.

I guess it’s hard to separate because I’ve already been feeling low energy most days, so sometimes the next day is still bad, but I don’t know that it’s a delayed reaction to activity. I haven’t been tracking it that closely, though.
Before these past two months, was there ever another time in your life when you felt depressed and lost interest in things nearly every day for at least two weeks?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I’ve had low periods before, like times where I felt really discouraged or kind of flat, but I don’t know if I can confidently say it was depressed and losing interest in things nearly every day for two full weeks.

Part of the problem is I don’t think I tracked it that way at the time. I’d usually just think, “I’m stressed,” or “I’m in a rut,” or “I need to get through this week,” and then I’d sort of keep going. Looking back, some stretches probably felt heavy, but I’m not sure whether they met that kind of consistent, almost every day pattern you’re asking about.

So… I guess my honest answer is I don’t know. I can’t point to a clear earlier episode the way I can with these past couple of months.
Have other people commented that you seem to be moving or speaking more slowly lately?

Yeah… my husband has noticed it, actually. He’s said a few times that I seem like I’m moving around the house like I’m underwater, which was kind of hard to hear because I didn’t realize it looked that obvious from the outside.

And with talking, too—he’ll ask me something really simple, like where something is or what I want to do about dinner, and I can feel there’s this lag. Like I know I should answer, but it takes me a while to get the words together, and then when I do answer, they come out slowly. He’s pointed that out more than once lately.
At any time before these past two months, was there ever a period when you felt depressed or lost interest in things nearly every day for at least two weeks?

I know you asked that a minute ago, and I’m sorry, I’m probably circling around it because I don’t have a clean answer.

I can’t really identify a definite earlier period where I’d say, yes, I was depressed or lost interest in things nearly every day for at least two weeks. I’ve had rough patches before, definitely—times where I felt worn down or unmotivated or like I was just pushing through—but when I try to look back and apply that “nearly every day for two weeks” standard, it gets fuzzy.

At the time, I don’t think I would have described it that way. I probably would’ve said I was stressed, or tired, or overwhelmed. And I wasn’t keeping track of whether it was every day or how long it lasted. So I don’t want to say yes if I’m just guessing. I guess the most honest answer is: I’m not sure, but I can’t point to a clear episode before these last couple of months.
Have you been sleeping more than usual lately?

I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’d say I’ve been sleeping more, exactly.

It’s a little hard to judge because my schedule has felt kind of blurred lately, and I’m not always great at keeping track of the hours. Some days I might stay in bed longer, but I don’t know if that means I’m actually sleeping more or just… not getting up right away. So if you mean actual hours asleep, I haven’t clearly noticed that increasing.
Have you gained weight مؤخراً without trying?

I don’t think so… at least, not that I’ve noticed in any clear way.

I haven’t been weighing myself regularly, so I can’t give you a number. My clothes don’t feel dramatically different or anything like that. I mean, some days I feel kind of uncomfortable in my body, but I don’t know if that’s actual weight gain or just how I’m feeling. So I wouldn’t want to say yes without really knowing.
At work or at home, have other people besides your husband noticed that you seem slowed down lately?

I don’t know if anyone at work has noticed, or if they have, they haven’t said anything to me directly. I’ve been trying to sort of keep it together there, so maybe people just think I’m quiet or tired.

At home, though, yes—my husband has definitely noticed. He’s said a few times that I’m moving around the house like I’m underwater, which sounds dramatic, but I kind of know what he means. Like I’ll be getting up to do something simple, or walking from one room to another, and it’s just… slow. Everything feels like it takes extra effort.

And when he asks me something really basic, like where something is or what I want to do about dinner, it can take me a while to answer. Not because I’m trying to be difficult. It’s like the words are there somewhere, but they come out so slowly, and there’s this lag before I respond. He’ll sometimes look at me like he’s waiting for me to finish loading, basically. So yes, he’s noticed it at home.
Have you been feeling worthless or excessively guilty lately?

Yes… I think so. I mean, “worthless” feels like a strong word, but I do keep getting stuck in this loop where I feel like I’ve done something really wrong.

It’s mostly about the mortgage decision. I keep replaying it over and over in my head, like I’m reviewing evidence against myself. I’ll think, why did I agree to that, why didn’t I slow everything down, why wasn’t I more careful? And then it turns into this feeling that I was selfish and reckless, like I put our whole household at risk because I wanted… I don’t even know, stability, or the house, or to move forward. But in my head it becomes this awful thing, like I endangered us.

My husband keeps reminding me that we made that decision together, that it wasn’t just me, and logically I know that. I can say the words. But it doesn’t really land. I still feel like I should have known better, or protected us somehow. I keep thinking, if something goes wrong, it’ll be my fault. So yes, there’s definitely guilt. More than makes sense, probably.
Before these past two months, was there ever a time when you felt this same kind of depressed mood and loss of interest nearly every day for at least two weeks?

I’m not sure about before this, honestly. What I can say is that this current depressed, slowed-down, exhausted feeling has been going on most days for about the past two months.

Before that, I don’t think I had this same thing in the same steady way, like nearly every day for two weeks or more—but I’d have to think back carefully. This one feels pretty continuous, though. It’s not just a bad few days. It’s been this kind of heavy stretch where most days I feel low and like I’m dragging myself through everything, and that’s been around two months now.
Have you been constipated lately?

I’m not really sure. I haven’t been tracking that closely, honestly. Nothing has jumped out at me as a big change, or like something I’ve been worried about.

I mean, some days my routine is off, but I don’t know that I’d call it constipation. It’s not something I’ve specifically noticed in the way you’re asking, I guess.

It’s more like… I notice when I’m already worn down, my thoughts can get more repetitive, like I’ll go over what I still need to do or whether I’m falling behind. But I’m not sure if that’s worry in the way you mean, or just me trying to keep track of everything and feeling like I don’t have enough bandwidth.

So I guess my answer is: maybe a little at times, but I haven’t really noticed a major increase in worrying about lots of different areas.

inference.note: F41.1 is less likely because the patient does not report pervasive/excessive worry across multiple domains. Depression remains strongly supported; neurasthenia/CFS-spectrum and hypothyroidism remain possible contributors to fatigue/nonrestorative sleep.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the current depressive episode has lasted at least two weeks, which is essential for diagnosing major depressive disorder and helps distinguish it from neurasthenia/chronic fatigue-related conditions or hypothyroidism.
doctor.question: How long have you been feeling this depressed and drained most days?

target_item.name: Depressive Episode Duration
target_item.manifestation: The depressed, slowed-down, exhausted part has been going on most days for about the past two months.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about how long the current depressed and drained state has been present most days.

patient.answer:
I’d say it’s been about two months now, most days. It didn’t feel like it started all at once, like one morning I woke up and everything was different, but looking back, that’s about when this depressed, slowed-down, drained feeling really became the usual.

At first I think I kept telling myself it was just a rough week, or that I was tired from work, or maybe I just needed a weekend to catch up. But then the weekends didn’t really reset anything, and the next week would start and I’d still feel the same. So… yeah, about the past two months is probably the clearest answer. Most days during that time I’ve felt low and just kind of exhausted in a way that feels hard to push through.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether there is a discrete, prolonged worsening of symptoms after exertion, which best distinguishes chronic fatigue syndrome from a depressive episode.
doctor.question: After even mild physical or mental activity, do you often have a delayed crash where your exhaustion gets clearly worse and lasts into the next day or longer?

target_item.reason: The question is specifically about delayed post-exertional worsening of exhaustion lasting into the next day or longer, which is not described in the symptom profile.

patient.answer:
I don’t think I’ve noticed that pattern, no. I definitely get tired after doing things, especially if I’ve already been feeling drained that day, but I’m not sure I’d call it a delayed crash.

Like, if I have a busy workday or I have to concentrate for a long stretch, I might feel more worn out afterward, but it seems more immediate or just part of the same general exhaustion. I can’t really point to a clear thing where I do something mild—like a short errand or a bit of mental effort—and then the next day I’m dramatically worse because of that specific activity.

I guess it’s hard to separate because I’ve already been feeling low energy most days, so sometimes the next day is still bad, but I don’t know that it’s a delayed reaction to activity. I haven’t been tracking it that closely, though.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether there have been distinct past depressive episodes, to distinguish recurrent major depressive disorder from a single current major depressive episode and from non-depressive fatigue syndromes.
doctor.question: Before these past two months, was there ever another time in your life when you felt depressed and lost interest in things nearly every day for at least two weeks?

target_item.reason: The question asks about any prior depressive episodes before the current past two months, but the symptom profile only describes the current depressive period and does not provide information about earlier lifetime episodes.

patient.answer:
I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, I’ve had low periods before, like times where I felt really discouraged or kind of flat, but I don’t know if I can confidently say it was depressed and losing interest in things nearly every day for two full weeks.

Part of the problem is I don’t think I tracked it that way at the time. I’d usually just think, “I’m stressed,” or “I’m in a rut,” or “I need to get through this week,” and then I’d sort of keep going. Looking back, some stretches probably felt heavy, but I’m not sure whether they met that kind of consistent, almost every day pattern you’re asking about.

So… I guess my honest answer is I don’t know. I can’t point to a clear earlier episode the way I can with these past couple of months.

doctor.intent: Assess whether there is psychomotor slowing, which would strengthen major depressive episode over neurasthenia, chronic fatigue syndrome, or hypothyroidism.

patient.answer:
Yeah… my husband has noticed it, actually. He’s said a few times that I seem like I’m moving around the house like I’m underwater, which was kind of hard to hear because I didn’t realize it looked that obvious from the outside.

And with talking, too—he’ll ask me something really simple, like where something is or what I want to do about dinner, and I can feel there’s this lag. Like I know I should answer, but it takes me a while to get the words together, and then when I do answer, they come out slowly. He’s pointed that out more than once lately.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether there has been a prior distinct major depressive episode to distinguish single-episode major depression from recurrent major depression.
doctor.question: At any time before these past two months, was there ever a period when you felt depressed or lost interest in things nearly every day for at least two weeks?

target_item.reason: The question asks about whether there was a prior depressive episode before the past two months; the provided profile covers current depressive symptoms and durations but does not include a separate past episode history.

patient.answer:
I know you asked that a minute ago, and I’m sorry, I’m probably circling around it because I don’t have a clean answer.

I can’t really identify a definite earlier period where I’d say, yes, I was depressed or lost interest in things nearly every day for at least two weeks. I’ve had rough patches before, definitely—times where I felt worn down or unmotivated or like I was just pushing through—but when I try to look back and apply that “nearly every day for two weeks” standard, it gets fuzzy.

At the time, I don’t think I would have described it that way. I probably would’ve said I was stressed, or tired, or overwhelmed. And I wasn’t keeping track of whether it was every day or how long it lasted. So I don’t want to say yes if I’m just guessing. I guess the most honest answer is: I’m not sure, but I can’t point to a clear episode before these last couple of months.

doctor.intent: Assess whether hypersomnia is present as a depressive neurovegetative symptom to help distinguish a major depressive episode from neurasthenia/chronic fatigue-related conditions and hypothyroidism.

target_item.reason: The question is directly about sleeping more than usual/hypersomnia, and the provided symptom profile does not include a sleep disturbance item.

patient.answer:
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’d say I’ve been sleeping more, exactly.

It’s a little hard to judge because my schedule has felt kind of blurred lately, and I’m not always great at keeping track of the hours. Some days I might stay in bed longer, but I don’t know if that means I’m actually sleeping more or just… not getting up right away. So if you mean actual hours asleep, I haven’t clearly noticed that increasing.

doctor.intent: Assess for weight gain as a key hypothyroid feature to help distinguish hypothyroidism from a primary depressive episode.

patient.answer:
I don’t think so… at least, not that I’ve noticed in any clear way.

I haven’t been weighing myself regularly, so I can’t give you a number. My clothes don’t feel dramatically different or anything like that. I mean, some days I feel kind of uncomfortable in my body, but I don’t know if that’s actual weight gain or just how I’m feeling. So I wouldn’t want to say yes without really knowing.

doctor.intent: Assess whether there is objective psychomotor slowing to further support a major depressive episode over hypothyroidism, neurasthenia, or chronic fatigue syndrome.
doctor.question: At work or at home, have other people besides your husband noticed that you seem slowed down lately?

target_item.name: Psychomotor_Changes
target_item.manifestation: My husband has pointed out that I move around the house like I am underwater, and when he asks me something simple it can take me a while to answer because the words come out so slowly.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether others have noticed the patient seeming slowed down, which directly refers to observable psychomotor slowing.

patient.answer:
I don’t know if anyone at work has noticed, or if they have, they haven’t said anything to me directly. I’ve been trying to sort of keep it together there, so maybe people just think I’m quiet or tired.

At home, though, yes—my husband has definitely noticed. He’s said a few times that I’m moving around the house like I’m underwater, which sounds dramatic, but I kind of know what he means. Like I’ll be getting up to do something simple, or walking from one room to another, and it’s just… slow. Everything feels like it takes extra effort.

And when he asks me something really basic, like where something is or what I want to do about dinner, it can take me a while to answer. Not because I’m trying to be difficult. It’s like the words are there somewhere, but they come out so slowly, and there’s this lag before I respond. He’ll sometimes look at me like he’s waiting for me to finish loading, basically. So yes, he’s noticed it at home.

doctor.intent: Assess low self-worth/excessive guilt to help confirm a major depressive episode over fatigue syndromes or hypothyroidism.
doctor.question: Have you been feeling worthless or excessively guilty lately?

target_item.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
target_item.manifestation: I keep replaying the mortgage decision and telling myself I was selfish and reckless, like I put our whole household at risk even when my husband reminds me we made the decision together.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question is directly asking about feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt.

patient.answer:
Yes… I think so. I mean, “worthless” feels like a strong word, but I do keep getting stuck in this loop where I feel like I’ve done something really wrong.

It’s mostly about the mortgage decision. I keep replaying it over and over in my head, like I’m reviewing evidence against myself. I’ll think, why did I agree to that, why didn’t I slow everything down, why wasn’t I more careful? And then it turns into this feeling that I was selfish and reckless, like I put our whole household at risk because I wanted… I don’t even know, stability, or the house, or to move forward. But in my head it becomes this awful thing, like I endangered us.

My husband keeps reminding me that we made that decision together, that it wasn’t just me, and logically I know that. I can say the words. But it doesn’t really land. I still feel like I should have known better, or protected us somehow. I keep thinking, if something goes wrong, it’ll be my fault. So yes, there’s definitely guilt. More than makes sense, probably.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports about two months of persistent depressed mood and clear loss of interest/pleasure, with recurrent thoughts that life is not worth living, excessive guilt/worthlessness, psychomotor slowing observed by her husband, and marked fatigue. This satisfies a current major depressive episode. Prior distinct depressive episodes were not established, so recurrent depressive disorder is not confirmed. Chronic fatigue syndrome is less likely because the fatigue occurs in the context of a syndromal depressive episode, unrefreshing sleep is present but the characteristic delayed post-exertional worsening was denied, and neurasthenia is less supported because prominent depressive syndrome is present.
